proof_nl:
Let n>1 be fixed, let t be real with 0<=t<1, and set a=floor(n t). Then by definition of the floor function,
a <= n t < a+1,
so dividing by n gives
a/n <= t < (a+1)/n.
In particular, t >= a/n.

Now for each k=1,...,n, since k>0 we have k t >= k(a/n), and the floor function is monotone increasing, hence
floor(k t) >= floor(k a/n).
Dividing by the positive integer k preserves the inequality:
floor(k t)/k >= floor(k a/n)/k.
Summing over k=1,...,n yields
sum_{k=1}^n floor(k t)/k >= sum_{k=1}^n floor(k a/n)/k.

Also, because a/n is a real number with n(a/n)=a, we have
floor(n(a/n)) = a = floor(n t).
Therefore
E_n(t) = floor(n t) - sum_{k=1}^n floor(k t)/k
<= a - sum_{k=1}^n floor(k a/n)/k
= E_n(a/n).
This is exactly the desired inequality.
solver_summary: Using a=floor(nt), we get t>=a/n. Monotonicity of floor gives floor(kt) >= floor(ka/n) for each k, so the weighted sum in E_n(t) is at least the corresponding sum at a/n. The leading floor(nt) term equals floor(n(a/n))=a, hence E_n(t) <= E_n(a/n).
vetter_reason: The argument correctly fixes n and an arbitrary t in [0,1), defines a=floor(nt), and proves E_n(t) <= E_n(a/n) by termwise monotonicity of floor under multiplication by positive k, followed by summation. The conclusion matches the lemma exactly and no forbidden dependencies are used.
